tb21_profile.skill: Write a .proto service definition with exact message/field names, run grpc_tools.protoc codegen, implement the generated servicer class, bind it to a port and keep it serving in the background
tb21_profile.domain: gRPC and Protocol Buffers in Python — grpcio/grpcio-tools install, _pb2/_pb2_grpc modules, service stubs, RPC server lifecycle
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec plus build/codegen: produce named artifacts from a schema and leave a working server running

searches: tools.py search tw "RPC|generate .* (code|bindings|stubs)|code generation|swagger|OpenAPI|thrift|socket server|listen on port|client and server" -n 25

notes: TMax is overwhelmingly the right pool: it has roughly fifty Python-gRPC tasks that author a .proto, run grpc_tools.protoc, implement the servicer and serve on a port, several of which are close to verbatim matches, so nine of the final ten are TMax. RTS's only relevant material is a ~15-way near-duplicate family that builds and runs a prebuilt Go gRPC server and calls it from Python — real domain overlap, little authoring skill; I took the two variants that add 'confirm it is listening' and 'verify the generated artifacts'. TerminalWorld has exactly one gRPC task (tw_285202) and SWE-Smith exactly one protobuf mention, so those lists fall back on the nearest transferable skills: pyasn1's schema-driven binary codec for SWE-Smith, and serialization/RPC libraries (pyserde, msgspec, osbrain, pymodbus, tfds protobuf) for SWE-Rebench. Retrieval trap: 'protocol' matched hundreds of RTS firewall tasks (protocol=tcp) and 'proto' matched pickle protocol versions; all discarded.
